prosecution_strengths: Higher degrees apply for use of weapon or persistent conduct.
Recorded communications provide direct evidence.
Victim testimony about fear is sympathetic.
defense_opportunities: Challenge whether statement was a 'true threat.'
common_defenses: Protected speech — not a true threat.
Hyperbole — venting, not actual threat.
No intent to threaten — statement was joke.
No reasonable fear — would not cause reasonable person to fear.

prosecution_strengths: Transcripts and recordings document statements.
Materiality is often clear from context.
common_defenses: Literally true — statement was technically accurate.
Not material — false statement not material.
Mistake — misunderstood the question.
Good faith — believed statement was true.

prosecution_strengths: Higher degrees escalate based on amount and position.
Wiretaps and undercover operations capture transactions.
Financial records trace payments.
common_defenses: Lawful payment — campaign contribution or legitimate payment.
No corrupt intent — not intended to influence official action.
Entrapment — induced by law enforcement.
Unreliable cooperator — fabricated allegations.

prosecution_strengths: Institutional records document custody.
Surveillance captures escape.
Additional charges may apply for offenses during escape.
common_defenses: Duress — faced imminent threats.
Not in custody — was not in lawful custody.
Prompt return — voluntarily returned.
Conditions defense — intolerable conditions.

prosecution_strengths: Veterinary testimony is compelling.
Photographic evidence is emotionally powerful.
Public sympathy for animal victims.
common_defenses: Lack of knowledge — unaware of condition.
Medical cause — illness not abuse.
Proper care — provided adequate care.
Agricultural exemption — within accepted practices.

prosecution_strengths: Probation officer testimony is persuasive.
Drug tests and missed appointments are objective.
Original sentence may be imposed upon revocation.
common_defenses: Substantial compliance — largely followed conditions.
Inability to comply — circumstances prevented compliance.
Technical violation — minor and not warranting revocation.
Inaccurate report — officer's report is incorrect.

prosecution_strengths: Parole officer testimony is primary evidence.
Electronic monitoring and drug tests provide objective evidence.
New criminal conduct is strong grounds.
common_defenses: Substantial compliance — largely complied.
Inaccurate evidence — drug tests or monitoring unreliable.
Circumstances beyond control — external factors.
Rehabilitation progress — has made significant progress.

prosecution_strengths: Evidence of planning, assistance, or encouragement establishes liability.
Co-defendant testimony is primary tool.
Conduct before/during/after crime demonstrates accomplice status.
common_defenses: Mere presence — was present but did not participate.
Withdrawal — withdrew before crime and took preventive action.
Lack of knowledge — did not know crime was planned.
Unreliable co-defendant — testimony fabricated.

prosecution_strengths: Statements about intentions are direct evidence.
Preparation evidence supports the charge.
Even significant attempts carry serious penalties.
defense_opportunities: Challenge whether actions were beyond mere preparation.
common_defenses: Mere preparation — actions did not constitute substantial step.
Voluntary renunciation — voluntarily and completely abandoned.
No intent — did not actually intend completed crime.
Equivocal conduct — actions did not corroborate criminal purpose.

prosecution_strengths: Higher degrees escalate based on type of conspiracy.
Communications document agreements.
Co-conspirator statements admissible against all members.
defense_opportunities: Argue lack of knowledge of criminal nature.
common_defenses: No agreement — parallel conduct does not prove conspiracy.
Withdrawal — withdrew and prevented the crime.
Lack of knowledge — was unaware of criminal nature.
Mere association — knew co-conspirators but did not agree.
